Wrong metric recorder for legacy DeleteCollection in goroutine - d.Legacy.DeleteCollection duration is recorded with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, causing legacy metrics to appear as storage metrics

The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.

Async goroutines derive child contexts from the request context, which may already be cancelled by the time the goroutine executes since the handler returns immediately after spawning the goroutine, causing legacy writes to fail silently
Failures in the background legacy write only go into a metric with no logging, and the goroutine has no panic recovery.
DeleteCollection goroutine (line 166): calls recordStorageDuration for the legacy operation — should be recordLegacyDuration

Async legacy writes are tied to request cancellation - background legacy operations inherit the request context, so if the request ends quickly the legacy write can be canceled immediately

In TestMode3_Create, the failing case only stubs Legacy.Create, but Mode3 calls Storage.Create first; without a storage expectation this won't exercise the intended error path (and may panic due to an unexpected mock call)

The async legacy Update reuses the original objInfo; since Storage.Update already applied the update, calling Legacy.Update with the same UpdatedObjectInfo can compute a different object or run update logic twice
The async legacy Create uses obj (the pre-storage object) rather than created returned by unified storage, which can drop server-assigned fields and cause legacy/unified divergence
